title: Area Separation LoRA [LORA/Anima]
description:
Where mix-ups come from


Diffusion models connect words to image areas through **cross-attention**. At every step, every position of the
image "looks at" the prompt's words and takes in some of each. If "dog" and "cat" pull on the same positions, the
model draws a mixture: a cat-dog, a dog's head on a person, or colours that land on the wrong thing ("purple"
meant for the teapot ends up on the apron).

You can see this attention directly. The act-steer extension for Forge records, for every word, how much of
the attention each image area gave it, and shows it as a **word map** above the image:

- **all words**: every area is tinted in the colour of the word that dominates it. The coloured chips under the
image are the prompt's words in their colours; grey words are filler words.

"I am sworn to carry your burdens."

## About

Lydia, the Whiterun housecarl, trained on in-game screenshots in her Steel Armor (her default outfit).

- Trigger word: Lydia-Skyrim (put it first, followed by 1girl, female_focus)

- Strength: 0.7 – 1.0 (0.9 recommended)

- Recommended epoch: the published file (epoch 6). Epochs 5–6 give the most faithful armor.

- Base model: Anima 2B (28 blocks): anima-base, oneObsession Anima v4, oneObsession mature Anima, homos

title: Slider: Background Sharpness/Blur [LORA/MOSS Image]
description:
Slider controlling background focus.

Dataset is composed of 100 images, 50% photo, 50% illustrations.

Usage:

- Positive: sharper, more detailed backgrounds.

- Negative: softer, out-of-focus backgrounds.

"Limitations":

Due to the way it is trained (predicting the difference between 3 different captions) it will change the image a bit.

Higher/Lower values will shift the composition a little. The model may add extra background detail such as people or signage, or zoom in on the subject.

Might sharpen and blur the subject itself a bit depending on the slider side.

title: One prompt → one song → a two-scene music video (YuE2 × MiniMax H3) [Workflows/MiniMax H3]
description:
Score to Screen — One prompt → one song → a music video (YuE2 × MiniMax H3)

Write one prompt and pick your images. You get an original song made with YuE2 and a music video made with MiniMax H3. The singer lip-syncs, the band plays along with the music, and every scene change lands exactly on a bar line.

🎞 v7.0: one screen for the whole MV. The 🎞 Timeline gets a left column with four tabs (🎬 Main, 🎵 Song, 🎚 Sound, ⚙ Settings) and can fill the whole window: 🎭 a cast of up to four people with their pictures, picked per scene, 🎵 the song in its own field, 🎚 the finished MV's sound (EQ, reverb, width, fades) with 🔁 remaking only the sound, and ⚙ models, LoRAs and VAEs in one place. Plus 🎸🎻 the hands play along: the fretting hand changes chord shape on the score's chord changes, a violinist's bow and fingers follow the note lengths, and the camera moves in to the fingers when a solo starts.

🥁 v6.

title: Anima-Role-Ref-KV [LORA/Anima]
description:
Anima Role Ref KV · v1.0

Generate new poses, outfits, expressions, and scenes from a character reference image and a text prompt, while keeping the character recognizable.

NSFW content was filtered out of the training data and was not used to train this release.

For ComfyUI · Requires Anima Base v1.0. Place the weights in ComfyUI/models/loras/. Download the required custom node and workflow from [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/AnticPan/Anima-Role-Ref-KV), restart ComfyUI, import the workflow, upload a reference, and Queue. The Anima Role Ref KV node loads the adapter itself.

Suggested settings: 28 steps, CFG 4, BF16, around 1 megapixel.

Try 1024 × 1024, 832 × 1216, or 1216 × 832; dimensions must be divisible by 16.

No trigger word is required.
